acceptanceCriteria: Each of the seven listed memories is classified with its chosen layer (product change, refusal text, helper/make target, check, or out-of-repository host limit) and the reason a lower layer was not chosen.
Every in-repository item has a merged change or its own filed ticket, and each merged change has a test or check that fails on the original friction.
The owner deletes or shortens each memory whose workaround is no longer needed, and the remaining memories name the ticket that would retire them.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from an owner-requested review of michael-denyer/pstack-claude (lesson: encode a repeated lesson in structure, not in more instruction text). Claude Code sessions on this machine carry per-project memory files that exist only to work around Corvint, Corvint Tasks or shell friction, and each new session re-reads them and still trips on the first attempt. Current workaround memories (~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/memory/): (1) corvint-tasks-payload-canonical: mutations refuse non-canonical JSON (key order, whitespace, unsorted set arrays) instead of canonicalizing or naming the exact fix; (2) corvint-tasks-ticket-create-payload: create needs all 20 closed keys with no emitted template, and enum values (kind, effects.coverage) are discovered by MALFORMED refusals; (3) corvint-tasks-intent-branch and corvint-taskman-store-routing: mutations need the primary checkout HEAD on main, and the projection carry from a feature branch is a manual multi-step recipe; (4) line-citations-check-reads-head: the doc citation check reads HEAD, so uncommitted edits are checked against stale content; (5) dogfood-bind-amend-breaks-trace: amending after the first bind pass breaks the trace store; (6) interactive-rm-cp-aliases: zsh rm/cp aliases prompt and hang non-interactive agent shells, so repo scripts must call command rm/cp; (7) codex-cli-headless-lanes: the required Codex model flag and the draft-PR refusal hook. Related: V1-0242 (route future friction to the earliest preventing layer) covers the policy; this ticket is the concrete backlog of existing memories. Each item should land at the earliest layer that removes it: product behavior or a clearer refusal, a repository helper or make target, a check, or a documented host limit when nothing in this repository can fix it.

AC1: docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0720-memory-workaround-layers.md classifies all seven memories by layer (product change, refusal text, helper/make target, check, or out-of-repository host limit) with the reason a lower layer was not chosen. AC2: the only in-repository product change, the DCG-V0-021 unstaged-edit note in script/check-line-citations.sh, is pinned by test case 21 in script/check-line-citations_test.sh, which fails against the previous script; the remaining in-repository items are filed as V1-0750, V1-0751 and existing V1-0325. AC3: on 2026-10-04 the owner approved and had applied the memory changes: line-citations-check-reads-head replaced by line-citations-check-reads-index without the HEAD and commit-first claims; dogfood-bind-amend-breaks-trace shortened to the refusal's named recovery; corvint-tasks-payload-canonical names V1-0750; corvint-tasks-ticket-create-payload names V1-0751 and drops the enum notes; corvint-tasks-intent-branch and corvint-taskman-store-routing name V1-0325; the rm/cp alias and Codex host-limit memories are kept. Re-verified 2026-10-04 on main cd70ba0ab538a612a13d146934cf95ef356c333d: make line-citations-test passed.
